summary: Hold some data back. The score on data the model never saw is the one to believe.
headline: Grade it on questions it has not seen
overview: Fit the model on one part of the data and keep the rest locked away. The held-back part is a rehearsal for the real world.
Notice how much the score moves when you re-split. One split gives one opinion, and a small test set gives a noisy one.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Score the model on its own training data. It looks far better, because it has already seen those points.

check.question: Your model scores very well on the data it was trained on. What does that tell you about new data?

realLife: A model graded on its own homework passes every exam in a notebook and fails in production.
data: Forty points from a noisy sine wave. A degree-5 polynomial is fitted to the training part each time. The strip under the plot shows the test error from 40 different random splits at the chosen size.
maths: test error = mean (ŷ − y)² over held-back rows only
The model never uses test rows to choose weights, settings or features.
Smaller test sets give noisier scores. Smaller training sets give a weaker model. The split size trades one against the other.
code:
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
Xtr, Xte, ytr, yte = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=0)
m = model.fit(Xtr, ytr)
print(m.score(Xte, yte))
